notes:
First attempt succeeded (200), no retries needed.

WATCH-1 (undeclared option-descriptor fields): CONFIRMED, partially. automation_state rows carry `value_category` (values: 'manual'/'automated'); status rows carry `colour` (equal to internal_name, e.g. 'active'/'draft'). priority and case_type rows carry NEITHER value_category nor colour — just internal_name/is_default/value/name. Neither `valueDetails` nor `entity_type` appears anywhere in this response (not on default_fields rows, not on custom_fields rows). None of these per-option fields (value_category, colour, internal_name, is_default) are declared in the schema at all — default_fields is documented only as an object with prose '{values, total_count}' and carries no item-level JSON-schema properties, so strictly everything inside each option row is 'undeclared'. automation_status has a distinct, simpler shape again ({name, value, is_default} only — no internal_name, no value_category) and guidance explicitly says it is 'assembled in this layer, not read from storage', which matches its odd-one-out shape.

WATCH-2 (duplicate option rows): CONFIRMED on this endpoint too. priority: 8 rows / 4 distinct values (Medium, Critical, High, Low), each name appearing exactly twice with different `value` ids (e.g. Medium: 318591 and 318618). status: 10 rows / 5 distinct values, same doubling pattern (e.g. Active: 318605 and 318632). case_type: 22 rows / 11 distinct values, same doubling pattern (e.g. Other: 318626 and 318599). In every duplicate pair, ALL other fields (internal_name, name, is_default, colour where present) are byte-identical between the two rows — the only difference is the `value` id. This endpoint exposes no `entity_type`, no `record_status`, and no per-option count field at all (only a list-level `total_count`), so it cannot itself confirm which of the two duplicate ids is the one 'carrying a real count' from the other probe's finding — it only corroborates that the same duplicate-id pattern exists at the project level (independent of whichever capability originally surfaced it). automation_state (5/5 distinct) and automation_status (5/5 distinct) show NO duplication — the doubling is specific to priority/status/case_type.

WATCH-3 (structural container mismatch): CONFIRMED, but on `system_fields`, not on custom_fields/default_fields. Schema declares system_fields as a bare `array` of {id, field_name, field_type, system_name, is_removable}. Actual response returns system_fields as an OBJECT: {description_fields: [...9 rows...], property_fields: [...10 rows...], others: []} — each sub-list holding the array-of-rows shape the schema described for the whole field. This is a genuine DRIFT: declared array, actual is a 3-key object of arrays.

WATCH-4 (prose vs schema disagreement): The capability's own guidance text says 'The response is three lists at the top level' (custom_fields, default_fields, system_fields) — this prose is itself wrong for system_fields (it's an object, not a list), independent of the JSON-schema's (also wrong) 'array' declaration. Both prose and schema agree system_fields should be array-shaped; reality disagrees with both. Separately, guidance's 'Each row carries links.self' is true for custom_fields rows and true for default_fields' top-level field groups (e.g. priority.links.self = '/api/v1/projects/379335744/test-case/priority'), but not for individual option values inside a group's `values` array — consistent with a reasonable reading of 'row' as the field/group level, not the option-value level, so no disagreement there.

custom_fields for this project contains one leftover field from earlier probe activity (__probe_cf_1789735254346_renamed, field_string) — pool project data, not something this probe created; noted for completeness, does not affect the verdict.

All declared top-level required keys (success, custom_fields, default_fields, system_fields) and all declared required custom_fields item keys are present; no missing required fields. Verdict is DRIFT solely on the system_fields array-vs-object structural mismatch, plus the broader undeclared-shape situation in default_fields.
